label: Dei Filius incomprehensibility: infinite knowability and finite received understanding
summary: Target: root-reaching bare bridge InfiniteIsIncomprehensible, currently ∀g, Infinite g -> Primitives.Incomprehensible g. Read the public translation of Aquinas ST I q.12 a.7 (https://www.newadvent.org/summa/1012.htm) and q.7 a.2 (https://www.newadvent.org/summa/1007.htm). No new source claim/pinned passage. Q12 a.7 supplies a specific reason: knowability follows actuality; infinite divine being is infinitely knowable; even an elevated CREATED intellect receives a finite degree of light of glory, so it cannot know the infinite being with the degree of adequacy that complete comprehension requires. This does NOT imply that a created intellect cannot know or see God at all: q.12 distinguishes vision from fully adequate comprehension. Q7 a.2 also recognizes that a created intellect has an 'infinite' reach in the extensional sense of understanding universals; therefore 'every created intellect has finite power' needs a sense restriction to received intensity/adequacy, not a general numerical or task-capacity bound. Proposed typed sibling: for each created intellect i, its attained degree of understanding g is bounded by its finite received intellectual light; infinite being g has knowability not exhausted by any such finite degree; Comprehends(i,g) entails attaining the full knowability of g. Those three separately explicit principles yield that no created intellect comprehends g. A further explicit sense bridge to Primitives.Incomprehensible, and a separate infinite-esse -> infinitely-knowable bridge, are OPEN. Do not identify Infinite g with unbounded knowledge by definition or equate 'incomprehensible' with wholly unknowable. Test with a created knower who really sees g but does not comprehend g, and ensure vacuity in a model with no created intellects is not counted as substantive warrant. This source-search and logical sketch create no Lean theorem and close no root premise.
blocker: Need typed created-intellect, received intellectual light, degree-of-understanding and full-comprehension senses; proof can then use an explicit no-finite-degree-exhausts-infinite condition. Q12 a.7 ad 1 also allows a broad sense of 'comprehension' as attaining/possessing what is sought; the proposed negative theorem uses ONLY strict exhaustive/adequate comprehension, not that broader sense. The metaphysical mapping from Infinite in esse to infinite knowability remains OPEN. Pin/materialize ST I q.12 a.7/q.7 a.2 before adding a stating claim.
